text:
anya: Quick sync — ran into a parity hole: private deployments (VPC/offline) aren't emitting the eviction/lease telemetry we rely on for hosted/dedicated fallbacks. Apps see 'no eviction' and stay pinned.

devon: Oof. Do you have a repro or log?

anya: repro in staging private cluster. The runtime sidecar drops the eviction webhook when control-plane is disabled; no fallback to local audit events.

matt: This is the contract mismatch we feared. Private mode disables control-plane callbacks for compliance; our hosted fallback expects webhook + trace id.

sarah: Two quick paths: (1) shim that writes a local audit file and control-plane agent polls it (privacy-preserving), or (2) local pubsub sink that proxies minimal eviction signals to customer-controlled observability.

liam: (2) sounds like it leaks signals out. Customers will balk at any outbound to hosted endpoints.

matt: Right — tradeoffs:
- shim-poll (1): no egress, added latency for detection (poll interval). simpler auth but delayed fallback.
- proxied signal (2): near realtime, but requires auth handshake and explicit customer opt-in, plus KMS for signing.

anya: Example poll config snippet I tested: 
```yaml
# private-runtime.conf
eviction_poll_interval: 15s
emit_local_audit: true
control_plane_disabled: true
```
It produced consistent local events we can surface in console, but the routing layer still needs to treat local audit as authoritative for fallback decisions.

devon: If we take approach (1) we must update the routing policy to accept two trust-sources: control-plane-webhook OR local-audit-signed-by-runtime. Also need a signature format so ops can't spoof.

sarah: Agreed. Keep signature scheme simple: runtime signs with the node KMS key, verify via customer-provided public key (stored in FCD manifest). No cloud egress.

liam: Curious about SLO impact. Polling interval 15s might be fine for background batch jobs, but product/chat latency-sensitive routes expect near-instant fallback. How do we keep SLA?

matt: Idea: hybrid mode. Default to local-poll; if customer enables 'fast-eviction-proxy' (explicit flag), runtime will open an outbound TLS channel to a regional collector (mutual TLS). Collector only sees ephemeral eviction tokens (no model/data). This is opt-in.

anya: Actionable next steps:
- Create an RFC draft with the two modes (local-poll vs opt-in proxy) + signature scheme. (owner: anya)
- Update routing policy to accept local-audit signatures. (owner: devon)
- Add console UI checkbox and manifest flag for opt-in proxy + mTLS key exchange. (owner: product/sarah)

ops-bot: Deployed staging runtime image: runtime:v2026-03-22-eviction-proto to private cluster-3 (sha:abcd1234).

devon: I'll start the routing policy PR. Will add tests for signed-audit acceptance and replay protection.

matt: Need an ops playbook for customers that enable proxy: key rotation flow, audit export, and how to verify no model payload left the cluster.

liam: +1 on playbook. Also include a performance benchmark: time-to-fallback at 1s/5s/15s intervals.

anya: Thanks all — I'll drop an RFC link here when drafted. :raised_hands:
